source_text:
Αἱ δὲ νηστεῖαι ὑμῶν μὴ ἔστωσαν μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν. νηστεύουσι γὰρ δευτέρᾳ σαββάτων καὶ πέμπτῃ: ὑμεῖς δὲ νηστεύσατε τετράδα καὶ παρασκευήν.
μηδὲ προσεύχεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐκέλευσεν ὁ κύριος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ αὐτοῦ, οὕτω προσεύχεσθε: Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου, ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον, καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφίεμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν, καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ: ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.
τρὶς τῆς ἡμέρας οὕτω προσεύχεσθε.
thought_title: Fasting and prayer not like the hypocrites
orientation: The Didache has just finished instructing how to baptize and is now teaching the community how to fast and pray, contrasting their practice with that of the hypocrites.
pass_a_gloss: But the fasts of you let them not be with the hypocrites. For they fast [on the] second [day] of [the] week and [the] fifth; but you fast [on the] fourth [day] and [the] preparation [day]. Neither pray as the hypocrites, but as commanded the Lord in the gospel of him, thus pray: Father of us, the [one] in the heaven, let it be made holy the name of you, let it come the kingdom of you, let it be done the will of you as in heaven also upon earth; the bread of us the daily give to us today, and forgive to us the debt of us, as also we forgive to the debtors of us, and do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil [one]; because of you is the power and the glory into the ages. Three times of the day thus pray.

choices.why: The phrase literally means 'second of the week,' a Jewish way of naming Monday; keeping 'week' preserves the idiom.
The source uses the ordinal alone, implying 'fifth day of the week'; the gloss keeps the ordinal to stay literal.
The noun τετράς means the fourth day of the week; rendering it as 'fourth day' keeps the source's idiom.
Παρασκευή is the standard term for Friday, the day of preparation before the Sabbath; the literal rendering preserves the source's vocabulary.
The adjective is traditionally rendered 'daily' in the Lord's Prayer; it is the standard English equivalent.
The articular adjective can be read as masculine ('the evil one') or neuter ('evil'); the gloss chooses the masculine reading common in the tradition.

bible_refs.note: Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου, ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον, καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφίεμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν, καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ

pass_b_english: Do not fast with the hypocrites. They fast on the second day of the week and the fifth, but you are to fast on the fourth day and the preparation day.

Do not pray as the hypocrites do either. Pray as the Lord commanded in his gospel: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we also forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the power and the glory forever.”
Pray this way three times a day.

last_rejected.quote: Pray as the Lord commanded in his gospel
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς ἐκέλευσεν ὁ κύριος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: English omits 'his' modifying gospel, but 'the Lord' is correctly identified.
last_rejected.ruling: 'his gospel' is present in English; no omission. Mere misreading by first checker.

last_rejected.quote: your kingdom come, your will be done
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου
last_rejected.why: English adds 'your' before 'will be done' matching Matthew; source lacks second 'your'.
last_rejected.fix: your kingdom come, will be done as in heaven and on earth
last_rejected.ruling: English 'your will' is governed by 'your kingdom come' context; normal English pronominal carryover, not meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Source has 'from the evil [one/thing]'; 'evil one' personifies, but Greek article allows either.
last_rejected.ruling: 'τοῦ πονηροῦ' with article commonly means 'the evil one'; standard rendering within normal range, not mistranslation.
